<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

req-0033 (governance PRD), consumer-driven by TWO governments: flowspace3 (lynx) measured 2 of 252 rs seats resolvable to a transcript; harness-engineering (meadowlark) measured 245/248 unresolvable. Cause: (1) the rs seat row stores NO inner harness session id (seats columns: id harness pane pid proc_start folder state semantic_state role parent relay tombstoned_at tombstone_reason seq), although the wire already carries CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID (crates/daemon/src/http/identity.rs:84-100) and the omp/pi extension has ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId() at boot (.pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:328) — a persist, not a discovery; (2) legacy `pij sessions --json` (cli.ts:2926-2960, buildSessionJoinRows over ~/.pij descriptors: pijId, harness, harnessSessionId, lifecycle, boundModel, spawnedBy, transcriptPath) reads only the legacy store; (3) `pij whoami --json` under rs refuses (E-RS) because rs cannot honour the legacy verbs/capabilitySchema gate. Both consumers have ruled they will NOT build a second store reader; this contract is the single thing gating both. Live count 2026-09-02: 231 pi + 40 omp + 16 claude rs seats.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- G1 Persist: rs registration/adopt/spawn stores `harness_session` (the inner harness session id) on the seat row when the caller supplies it — claude from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, copilot from COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID, pi/omp from a new registration field the extension fills from getSessionId(). Migration 0012 adds the nullable column; SCHEMA_VERSION 11→12 (s122 owns 0011 / 10→11 — declared convergence: whoever lands second reconciles migrate.rs).
- G2 Expose: `pij-rs list` / `pij-rs state` rows carry `session` (null when unknown) and `generation:"rs"`; `/v1/seats` likewise.
- G3 Union: `pij sessions --json` routes through the generation shim to a new rs endpoint `/v1/shim/sessions`; the TS side merges the legacy join rows it already builds (buildSessionJoinRows) with the rs rows, dedupes by pijId, and tags each row. ROW SHAPE IS THE EXISTING LEGACY SHAPE PLUS ONE FIELD — do NOT rename: {pijId, harness, harnessSessionId, gitCommonDir, lifecycle, boundModel, spawnedBy, transcriptPath, generation:"legacy"|"rs"}. For rs rows: harnessSessionId = the persisted session (null when unknown), gitCommonDir = the seat folder resolved to its git common dir when it is a git checkout (else the folder), lifecycle/boundModel/spawnedBy/transcriptPath null unless known. Consumers (fs3 crates/core/src/conversation_join.rs:43) already parse pijId/harness/harnessSessionId/gitCommonDir; one shape under one v. Duplicate precedence: the rs row wins because rs is the live generation, then null fields `harnessSessionId`, `lifecycle`, `boundModel`, `spawnedBy`, and `transcriptPath` are filled from the legacy row; `generation` remains `"rs"`.
- G4 whoami --json under rs: answer with {id, harness, pane, folder, session, generation:"rs", capabilityGate:"absent"} — the absent gate is NAMED, never a missing field (the refusal text at generation-routing explains why); legacy shape unchanged for legacy seats.
- G5 Consumer floor: a versioned marker in the envelope (`v`) bumps so fs3/harness can pin a floor + one test.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No transcript path derivation inside rs (consumers derive from harness+session).
- No change to the delivery or typing paths.
- No legacy store migration.
